March 15, 33.

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your letter
dated February 21, 1933, on the subject of one George
Gregorieff alias George Gregory, and to state that he
arrived in Kobe from San Francisco on June 9, 1932 by
the s.s. "Taiyo Maru", and in Shanghai three days later.

While at Kobe, Gregorieff told the Police that
he intended to proceed to the U.S.S.R. for the purpose
of visiting his family and would apply at Shanghai for
a passport visa in order to be able to do so.

Subsequent to reaching Shanghai, Gregorieff
stated that he left Russia for San Francisco via
Vladivostock in 1930. He added that when coming to
Shanghai, he was not permitted to go ashore in Japan,
although he was in possession of a permit from the
Japanese Consulate in San Francisco authorizing him to
do so.

The passenger list of the s.s. "Taiyo Maru"
contains the following particulars regarding Gregorieff:
"George Gregory, 54, Journalist; home address,
1007, Rhode Island St., San Francisco; address
in Shanghai, 786, Avenue Joffre".

1933年3月17日

1933年3月15日。

先生：

谨提及贵处1933年2月21日关于乔治·格里戈里耶夫（又名乔治·格雷戈里）一事的来信，并告知：此人于1932年6月9日乘“太阳丸”号轮船（s.s. "Taiyo Maru"）从旧金山抵达神户，并于三天后抵达上海。

在神户期间，格里戈里耶夫向警方表示，他打算前往苏联探望家人，并将在上海申请护照签证以便成行。

抵达上海后，格里戈里耶夫称，他于1930年经海参崴离开俄罗斯前往旧金山。他还补充说，在来上海途中，尽管他持有旧金山日本领事馆签发的允许其上岸的许可证，但未被允许在日本上岸。

“太阳丸”号的乘客名单中包含以下关于格里戈里耶夫的信息：“乔治·格雷戈里，54岁，记者；家庭住址：旧金山罗德岛街1007号；上海住址：霞飞路786号”。

page_data.en:
-2-

The particulars given by Gregorieff at the
offices of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau on
June 13, 1932, are as follows:-

'George Gregorievitch Gregorieff, Russian, born
'January 18, 1878, at St. Petersburg; journalist
'and photographer; married; has three sons:
'Anatoly, Boris and Leonid aged respectively 19,
'16 and 14 years; holds passport No.2960 issued
'in December 1919 at Vladivostock; arrived in
'Shanghai from San Francisco on June 12, 1932;
'intends to proceed to Harbin via Dairen on
'June 18, to visit relatives and friends there;
'resides at No. 184, Range Road'.

Gregorieff left here for Dairen by the s.s.
"Dairen Maru" which sailed on June 18 and it is be-
lieved that it was his intention to go to Changchun.

Enquiries at No.792, Avenue Joffre (which
was formerly No.786) and No.184, Range Road, as well
as at the offices of the two local Russian Emigrants
Organisations, have failed to elicit any information
regarding G. Gregorieff or his daughter.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(Sd) F. W. Garrard
Commissioner of Police.

Edwin S. Cunningham, Esq.,
American Consul-General,
Shanghai.

-2-

格里戈里耶夫于1932年6月13日在上海公共租界巡捕房（Shanghai Public Safety Bureau）提供的详细信息如下：

“乔治·格里戈里耶维奇·格里戈里耶夫，俄国人，1878年1月18日出生于圣彼得堡；记者兼摄影师；已婚；有三个儿子：阿纳托利、鲍里斯和列昂尼德，年龄分别为19岁、16岁和14岁；持有1919年12月在海参崴签发的第2960号护照；于1932年6月12日从旧金山抵达上海；打算于6月18日经大连前往哈尔滨，探望那里的亲友；现居住在兰路184号”。

格里戈里耶夫于6月18日乘“大连丸”号轮船（s.s. "Dairen Maru"）离开此地前往大连，据信他的意图是前往长春。

经在霞飞路792号（原门牌号为786号）和兰路184号查询，并向当地两个俄国侨民组织办事处查询，均未获得有关G. 格里戈里耶夫或其女儿的任何信息。

谨此致意，
先生，
顺颂
时祺

（签名）F. W. 加拉德
警务处处长

埃德温·S·坎宁安 先生，
美国总领事，
上海。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

Subject (in full) Enquiry from the American Consulate-General re :
George Gregorieff alias George Gregory.

Made by D.S. Prokofiev. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the letter dated February 21,
1933 from the American Consulate-General on the subject of one
George Gregorieff alias George Gregory, enquiries show that
this individual arrived in Kobe from San Francisco on June 9,
1932 by the s.s. "Taiyo Maru." In a statement to the Kobe
police Gregorieff declared that he was proceeding to the
U.S.S.R. for the purpose of visiting his family there and
intended, upon arrival in Shanghai, to apply for a passport
vise to enable him to enter that country. He also stated that he
left Russia for San Francisco via Vladivostok in 1920.
Although he was in possession of a permit issued by the Japanese
Consular authorities in San Francisco to land in Japan, he
was not allowed to do so and proceeded to Shanghai by the same
vessel, arriving here on June 12, 1932.

The passenger list of the s.s. "Taiyo Maru"
contains the following particulars regarding this person :
George Gregory, 54, journalist; home address: 667 Rhode Island St.,
San Francisco; address in Shanghai - 726 Avenue Joffre.

The particulars given by him at the offices of the
Shanghai Public Safety Bureau on June 13, 1932 are as follows:
"George Gregorievitch Gregorieff, Russian, born
January 18, 1878, at St. Petersburg; journalist and photographer;
married; has three sons: Anatoly, Boris and Leonid aged respective-
ly 19, 16 and 14 years; holds passport No.2960 issued in
December 1919 at Vladivostok; arrived in Shanghai from San
Francisco on June 12, 1932; intends to proceed to Harbin
via Dairen on June 18, to visit relatives and friends there;
resides at No.154 Range Road."

参照美国总领事馆1933年2月21日关于乔治·格里戈里耶夫（又名乔治·格雷戈里）一事的来信，经查，此人于1932年6月9日乘“太阳丸”号轮船从旧金山抵达神户。在向神户警方所作的陈述中，格里戈里耶夫宣称他正前往苏联探望那里的家人，并打算在抵达上海后申请护照签证以便进入该国。他还表示，他于1920年经海参崴离开俄罗斯前往旧金山。尽管他持有旧金山日本领事当局签发的允许其在日本登陆的许可证，但未获准许，遂乘同一艘船前往上海，于1932年6月12日抵达此地。

“太阳丸”号的乘客名单中包含关于此人的以下信息：乔治·格雷戈里，54岁，记者；家庭住址：旧金山罗德岛街667号；上海住址——霞飞路726号。

他于1932年6月13日在上海公共租界巡捕房提供的详细信息如下：
“乔治·格里戈里耶维奇·格里戈里耶夫，俄国人，1878年1月18日出生于圣彼得堡；记者兼摄影师；已婚；有三个儿子：阿纳托利、鲍里斯和列昂尼德，年龄分别为19岁、16岁和14岁；持有1919年12月在海参崴签发的第2960号护照；于1932年6月12日从旧金山抵达上海；打算于6月18日经大连前往哈尔滨，探望那里的亲友；现居住在兰路154号。”

Shanghai, China, February 21, 1933.

DEPARTMENT OF STATE

Subject: George Gregorieff.

〔左侧手写批注：X see 0.12/.〕

Major F. W. Gerrard, C.I.E.,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
18 Hankow Road,
Shanghai, China.

Sir:

1/      I have the honor to enclose herewith a copy of
a letter from the Associated Charities of San
Francisco, dated October 22, 1932, requesting infor-
mation regarding the whereabouts and activities of
one George Gregorieff.

        Upon making inquiries, this office has learned
that Gregorieff departed from San Francisco on board
the S.S. TAIYO MARU on May 21, 1932, and left the
vessel upon arrival at Yokohama with the declared
intention of proceeding to Shanghai. He gave his
Shanghai address as 726 Avenue Joffre, which is
presumably the address of his daughter, who sent him
the money for his steamer passage.

        This office will appreciate any information
which you may be able to furnish regarding the pre-
sent address and activities of the man in question.

        I have the honor to be, Sir,
                Your obedient servant,

                Edwin S. Cunningham
                American Consul General.

ASSOCIATED CHARITIES OF SAN FRANCISCO
1010 Gough St.

October 22, 1932.

#53076

Re: George Gregorieff
Alias Gregory.

American Consulate,
Shanghai, China.

Gentlemen:

The above man left San Francisco in May of
this year to visit a daughter in Shanghai who had
sent him the necessary money for his ticket.

He left behind him an invalid wife and three
children who are being supported by the community
and the family tell us that they have had only one
letter from him and that was when the outgoing boat
reached Honolulu and they profess not to have the
name and address of the above mentioned daughter.

It is our understanding that Mr. Gregorieff
who undoubtedly obtained a permission for reentry
to the United States would have to report to you for
a visa upon arrival and that you therefore probably
would have his daughters address. If that is so,
we would be glad to have you forward it to us, also
any other possible information about Mr. Gregorieff.

We would like to add to the above that accord-
ing to reports from countrymen of Mr. Gregorieff
here in San Francisco Mr. Gregorieff is likely to
be an agent of the Soviets and that he may be em-
ployed in that capacity in Shanghai or elsewhere.

Appreciating your cooperation, we are

Yours very truly,

ASSOCIATED CHARITIES

By (Sgd.) M. Jorgensen
(Miss) M. Jorgensen

1932年10月22日。

#53076

事由：乔治·格里戈里耶夫
又名格雷戈里。

致：
中国上海美国领事馆。

诸位先生：

上述男子于今年五月离开旧金山，前往上海探望其女儿，其女曾寄给他购买船票所需的费用。

他留下了一位病残妻子和三个孩子，均由社区资助供养。其家属告诉我们，他们只收到过他一封信，那是当出港船只抵达火奴鲁鲁时寄出的，并且他们声称没有上述女儿的姓名和地址。

据我们了解，格里戈里耶夫先生无疑已获得重新进入美国的许可，因此在抵达时需向贵馆报告以申请签证，因此贵馆可能掌握其女儿的地址。如果是这样，我们恳请贵馆将该地址转发给我们，以及关于格里戈里耶夫先生的任何其他可能信息。

我们要补充的是，根据旧金山当地格里戈里耶夫先生的同胞提供的报告，格里戈里耶夫先生很可能是苏维埃代理人，并且可能在上海或其他地方以此身份受雇。

感谢合作，此致

敬礼

联合慈善协会

由 （签名）M. 约根森
